title: An Empirical Preregistered Evaluation of Generate–Validate–Repair for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑backed paired experiment (GVR-ProtocolEval-2026-PR1) that compared LLM-only configuration generation to a guarded generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline on intent‑to‑configuration NetOps tasks. Under a frozen plan we ran 200 stratified paired trials in a Dockerized Mininet emulator using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator. Observed confirmatory outcomes: baseline verifier‑accepted = 200/200; guarded verifier‑accepted = 200/200; paired contingency n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729); exact paired McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Crucially, the preregistered generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" produced a single LLM candidate per task that was scored under both arms (repair attempts therefore did not occur). The null paired difference documents this preregistered boundary condition (shared‑generation) rather than a general negative result about GVR utility. We publish the full preregistration, execution manifest, per‑episode LLM outputs, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, analysis artifacts and deterministic reconciliation with SHA‑256 hashes to enable deterministic reproduction and to support follow‑up experiments that relax the shared‑generation constraint.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation is operationally valuable but risky when generative models produce unsafe or inconsistent device changes. Generate–validate–repair (GVR) architectures pair a generative model with a deterministic validator and bounded repair loop to reduce deployment failures (reachability loss or policy violations). Prior work has explored LLMs for NetOps and verifier‑assisted pipelines, but comparisons frequently lack preregistration, deterministic artifact publication, or paired within‑task designs that control sampling variance. Our goal was a preregistered, artifact‑grounded paired comparison to quantify GVR benefit under a frozen emulator and validator and to publish all artifacts for exact reproduction.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and benchmarks examine LLMs for NetOps and AIOps, and verifier‑assisted approaches have been proposed (examples: NetConfEval; OpsEval; NetEval). Program repair and generate‑then‑validate literature in software engineering motivated our architectural framing. Unlike prior benchmarking runs, we preregistered the design, archived all artifacts, and ran a deterministic paired analysis with published hashes so the community can reproduce the exact execution and vary the boundary conditions.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. The preregistration (GVR-ProtocolEval-2026-PR1) froze research question, estimands, stratified paired sampling (200 confirmatory tasks), bootstrap parameters (10,000 resamples, seed 1729), contamination checks (≥80% token overlap exclusion), stopping rules, and generation semantics. Preregistration ID and SHA‑256: GVR-ProtocolEval-2026-PR1 (preregistration SHA‑256 d913b4167cc6aa85b283e0703e0bfff0c3e8864405f5159d9a1a1cf5fc3fafdc). System and artifacts. Adapter/orchestration: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Declared LLM: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json, SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Emulation & validator: Dockerized Mininet emulator and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (per‑episode scoring JSONs contain validator traces). Task bank and sampling. Confirmatory bank: 200 tasks stratified across protocol families and two modalities (CLI, API). Execution contract: generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (one LLM candidate produced per confirmatory task and evaluated under both baseline and guarded arms). This was preregistered and executed as recorded in execution/model_configuration.json (artifact hash above). Execution and archival. All raw LLM outputs, provider call traces, scoring JSONs, validator traces, execution manifest, and analysis artifacts were archived and hashed (execution manifest SHA‑256 d76af611272bd8e8b3a94290efecd6ecf634c5f3e36c2450c4245985e96931fb). Statistical analysis. Primary estimand: paired difference in binary operational‑failure indicator (1 if verifier finds reachability/policy failure; 0 otherwise). Inference: paired bootstrap percentile CI (10k resamples, seed 1729) and exact paired test (McNemar) per the preregistration.
sections.results: Execution summary. Planned episodes = 400 (200 tasks × 2 arms). Completed episodes = 400; model calls used = 200 (one shared generation per task); failed episodes = 0 (execution manifest SHA‑256 d76af611...). Scoring outcomes (analysis artifacts): baseline verifier‑accepted 200/200; guarded verifier‑accepted 200/200. Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a42b5...): n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Primary inference: paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00; bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729); exact paired (McNemar two‑sided) p = 1.0. Repair activity: per preregistered generation_semantics the same candidate was scored under both arms; repair_applied = false for all confirmatory episodes (see execution/scoring/*.json entries and representative artifacts: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 9235bce7..., execution/scoring/task-000002-guarded.json SHA‑256 25e2c0c7..., execution/scoring/task-000003-guarded.json SHA‑256 20e953b1...). Representative episodes and validator traces are archived (examples in evidence bundle).
sections.discussion: Interpretation. The confirmatory paired null result arises from a preregistered boundary choice: generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (one LLM output per task evaluated under both arms). That choice conserved model calls but mechanically prevented repair‑driven differences because no per‑arm independent generation or repair loop materialized. Therefore the executed run does not adjudicate the preregistered scientific question about repair efficacy in a setting where repairs can change acceptance; it demonstrates that under the shared‑generation boundary both arms accepted the same candidates. Evidence‑backed diagnostics. Contamination checks (automated token‑overlap ≥80% threshold) flagged no confirmatory exclusions (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA‑256 389227f0...). Validator traces in scoring JSONs show which syntactic and semantic checks exercised the candidate (see the representative scoring JSONs named above). Possible reasons for baseline=100% (nonexclusive): (1) the validator/emulator rule set and tasks (as encoded) permitted the generated candidates (validator coverage and task difficulty interact); (2) task templates were solvable and matched the LLM’s capabilities for this closed emulator; (3) the shared single draw happened to be successful for every task. The archived artifacts permit independent investigation of these hypotheses (provider traces, responses, validator logs, and per‑task manifests are all hashed and available). Threats to validity. Internal: the shared‑generation decision is an internal design choice that removed the repair intervention from observed confirmatory variance; readers must not conflate this boundary result with a general disproof of GVR. Construct: the deterministic validator measures a limited operational property (finite rule set); gaps in coverage change construct validity. External: single model (gpt‑5‑mini), synthetic task templates, and Mininet emulation limit generalizability to diverse vendors and production fleets. Consequences for interpretation and follow‑ups. To test the repair value of GVR experimentally, researchers should (A) set independent_condition_generation = true (one independent generation per arm) or sample multiple stochastic candidates per arm so repair loops may alter acceptance, and (B) expand validator coverage and emulator fidelity. All artifacts needed to perform these follow‑ups (task manifests, LLM outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest, deterministic reconciliation, analysis scripts) are archived and hashed to permit exact replication and principled extensions.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired experiment comparing LLM-only generation and a guarded GVR pipeline across 200 stratified NetOps tasks. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one LLM candidate per task scored under both arms) both arms achieved 100% verifier acceptance (n11=200), yielding a paired difference of 0.00 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed=1729). This outcome documents a preregistered boundary condition (shared candidate per task) rather than settling whether repairs improve outcomes when repairs are permitted to alter candidates. We publish the complete preregistration (SHA‑256 d913b416...), raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, execution manifest (SHA‑256 d76af611...), and analysis artifacts (paired contingency table SHA‑256 7bc1bd2a...) so others can reproduce the exact run and perform follow‑ups that relax the shared‑generation constraint or broaden model/validator scope.

Preregistered experiment elements executed autonomously after the lock: literature review, research‑gap selection, formal preregistration, task bank generation, code generation for the adapter harness, experiment execution, artifact archival and hashing, deterministic reconciliation, statistical analysis, autonomous peer review, and manuscript drafting and revision. limitations: Emulation and task scope: confirmatory bank used synthetic vendor‑like templates and a Dockerized Mininet emulator; production firmware/device heterogeneity and runtime complexity are not represented.

Single‑model, single‑draw design: only gpt-5-mini was used and generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" produced a single LLM candidate per task so repair_attempts = 0; thus the executed confirmatory run did not exercise repair loops.

Validator coverage: the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a finite rule set; untested operational properties (vendor firmware side effects, timing-dependent behaviors) remain outside the measured construct.

Power‑plan mismatch: the preregistered power calculation assumed nonzero baseline failure rates; the observed baseline success = 100% invalidates the preregistered MDE target and prevents demonstrating the originally planned effect size.

Contamination detection limits: automated token‑overlap checks flagged no confirmatory exclusions (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA‑256 389227f0...), but undiscoverable overlap between model pretraining data and task templates cannot be fully excluded.
External generalizability: results under the executed boundary conditions do not generalize to other models, sampling regimes, richer validators, or production heterogeneous device fleets.
